analysis: Examined two head-side excerpts of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (lines ~31297-32276 and 32277-33271). They contain only golden test vectors for the prompt contract: request_body, provider_body, template_input, plan (prompt_contract_id, token counts, block boundaries, chain hashes) and token_ids for gemma-4-26b-qat-4bit and gpt-oss-20b cases such as tool calls, unicode, Harmony framing and endpoint conversions. The patch excerpt shows the change adds additional_context.enable_thinking=false and shifts token counts and chain hashes. It is a data-only fixture change; no executable code, auth, attestation, key custody, encryption, WebSocket or billing logic is touched. No threat-model assets, boundaries or mitigations (TB-002, TB-011, T-041 cache) are weakened by the visible lines. Fixture content such as 'tool_choice' forced-call prompt text and harmony-framing strings in assistant content is test input, not a control. Remaining integration questions, outside the supplied evidence: (1) whether the Swift/Go code that generates prompt_contract_id and chain hashes changed in the same PR, since the new hashes imply a prompt-contract template change; (2) whether the cache-routing prefix hashes (T-041 cross-tenant prefix cache, cache_routing_eligible=true) remain scoped per scope_id and are not affected by the additional_context change; (3) whether the full patch beyond the truncated excerpt, covering other hunks at lines ~43739-54088, contains anything unexpected. Only the fixture is visible, so no regression is identified, but the corresponding source changes were not supplied. I set needs_deeper_review=false since nothing in the visible data affects a security conclusion.
